sentences.text: 1 3. Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2, the parties started residing separately since August, 2018.
Subsequently, respondent no.2/complainant lodged an FIR against the petitioners herein.
4. On 19.02.2022, parties arrived at a settlement vide Memorandum of Understanding/Compromise dated 19.02.2022 (Annexure P-2).

As per the said Memorandum of Understanding/Compromise,
petitioner no.1 has agreed to pay an amount of Rs. 14,00,000/- to the respondent no.2/wife towards full and final settlement of all her claims including istridhan, permanent alimony and maintenance - present, past and future.

5. In terms of the said settlement, the marriage between the parties stands dissolved by a decree of divorce dated 14.09.2022, passed by Ms. Seema Maini, learned Principal Judge, Family Court,
North-West District, Rohini Courts, Delhi (Annexure P-4).

sentences.text: Further, as per the said Memorandum of Understanding/Compromise, an amount of Rs. 10,00,000/- has already been paid to respondent no.2 and the remaining amount of Rs. 4,00,000/- has been paid to her in court today, by means of a demand draft.

6. Petitioners and complainant/respondent no. 2 are present before the Court and have been duly identified by their respective counsel, as well as the Investigating Officer, ASI Vikas Kumar, P.S.
Keshav Puram.

7. A demand draft bearing no. 001062, dated 24.08.2023, for Rs. 4,00,000/- drawn on Axis Bank,
Sector-8, Rohini, Delhi has been handed over to the complainant/Respondent No.2, who acknowledges the receipt of the same.

9. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.
